 Holding TSMC Near $352? Past Drops Went Deeper
 November 20th, 2026 · by Trefis Team TSM YTD +16.8% SPY YTD +5.8% QQQ YTD +5.4% Analyze TSM → Today’s big story: Will 2027 Be A 2022 Repeat For Stocks? 
 Stocks fell on Thursday, and the S&P 500 lost 2.0%. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) fell more than its big chip peers this week. Its US-listed shares closed at $352.09 on Thursday, Nov 19. That is down 11.7% in four trading days from last Friday’s close. No week since the one ending March 20, 2020 saw TSMC fall this much.
 So what happened after past weeks this bad? We found 16 earlier episodes since 1997. TSMC was higher 12 months later in 9 of them and lower in 7. But in 15 of the 16, the stock first fell further.
 Taiwan’s market fell even harder than TSMC this week. We measure it with the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF (EWT), a fund of Taiwanese stocks. It fell 13.8% from the Nov 13 close to the Nov 19 close. Only three weeks since June 2000 were worse for that fund.
 Image from Pixabay 
 How did TSMC do after each past week this bad?
 We counted every week since October 1997 in which TSMC fell at least 11.7%. Twenty-nine weeks qualify. Weeks that came within about three months of each other count as one episode. That leaves 16 episodes. Through Thursday’s close, this week ranks 30th worst of 1,519 weeks.
 The lowest close in the year after each bad week was a median 26.3% below that week’s close. The deepest further falls were 63.7% after the week ending Dec 21, 2001 and 61.7% after the week ending March 10, 2000.
 In 15 of its 16 past episodes, TSMC kept sliding after a week like this one, in the worst case by 63.7% within a year. If TSMC is a big part of your savings, that is a second drop you would have to sit through. When the market has fallen, the Trefis High Quality (HQ) Portfolio has lost about 81 cents for every $1 its benchmark lost, on average. See the HQ record .
 The rebounds were large when they came. The median return 12 months later was a gain of 55.7%. The table below shows every episode, its fall that week, the result a year later and the lowest point on the way.

Later returns start from that week’s close. A year here means 252 trading days. The last column is the lowest close in that year, measured against the same starting close.
 Here is the plain test. A week this bad was followed by a lower price a year later in 7 of 16 episodes. That is less than half. So a bad week has not been a reliable sign of more decline a year out.
 Why did some of those falls keep going?
 Most of the record is old. Thirteen of the 16 episodes came between 1997 and 2003. Since 2004 there were only three. TSMC was down 7.5% a year after the 2004 episode and up 63.1% a year after the 2008 one.
 Falling sales explain part of the worst cases. TSMC’s yearly revenue has dropped in only three years since 1997: 2001, 2009 and 2023. The worst was 2001, when it fell 21.7%. The two worst 2000 episodes led into that year.
 Sales do not explain everything, though. After the week ending Dec 21, 2001, the stock was down 49.4% a year later. Yet revenue grew in 2002. In the other direction, revenue fell 11.5% in 2009. The stock still rose 63.1% in the year after its October 2008 episode.
 Are TSMC’s sales falling with its price this time?
 No, not so far. TSMC’s revenue rose about 51% in the July to September quarter from a year earlier. Those figures are in Taiwan dollars, as TSMC reports them.
 Free cash flow is the cash left after running the business and paying for new plants and equipment. TSMC’s free cash flow rose 74.0% in the first nine months of 2026 from a year earlier. Analysts expect revenue to grow 38.6% in 2027. That average comes from 24 analysts.
 We could not tie TSMC’s fall to a company event. It fell with the wider market and other chip stocks, and our data does not show one cause for that. If sales and cash keep growing as analysts expect, that is the clearest reason buyers could return. If orders slow, the history above shows how much further the stock has fallen before.
 Did other chip stocks fall as much this week?
 TSMC fell more than its big chip peers from the Nov 13 close to the Nov 19 close. The broad market fell less than half as much.
 Nvidia fell 10.4%.
 ASML Holding fell 9.3%.
 Advanced Micro Devices fell 8.4%.
 Broadcom slipped 0.10%.
 The SPY fund, which holds S&P 500 stocks, fell 5.1%.
 For more on AI stocks, see the AI story we follow . For the market-wide version of this question, see Will 2027 Be A 2022 Repeat For Stocks? 
 What does the record mean for a TSMC owner now?
 Our read: the full record does not say to sell after a week like this. It does say the ride has usually got rougher before it got better. Today’s sales and cash look very different from 2001 so far.
 If TSMC has grown into a large share of your savings after its run to a record close of $485.80 on Oct 5, another slide would hit hard. It is easier to decide how much to keep, and when you would sell some, before the next drop than during it.
